metadata.note: The Auburn and Rochester Railroad, Rochester - Canandaigua - Geneva - Seneca Falls - Auburn, opened 1840-41 and the western half of the 'Auburn Road' between Rochester and Syracuse. Merged 1 Aug 1850 with the Auburn and Syracuse into the Rochester and Syracuse, consolidated into the New York Central in 1853; NYC passenger service ended 18 May 1958. Tourist trains returned to parts of it in 2025 (Finger Lakes Rail Experience). Seven features on shared geometry, split by operator (Rule 4): A&R 1840-1850 (Rochester - Canandaigua) and 1841-1850 (Canandaigua - Auburn); Rochester and Syracuse 1850-1853; New York Central 1853-1883 (to the original Mill St depot) and 1883-1958 (ending at the Brighton junction with the main line); Finger Lakes Rail Experience 2025 (Canandaigua - Geneva) and 2025-2026 (Waterloo - Aurelius). The eastern partner, Syracuse - Auburn, is data/auburn_and_syracuse_railroad.geojson. Research report: research/branches/auburn_and_rochester_railroad.txt.

metadata.ownership_split: Split 1 Aug 1850 (A&R -> Rochester and Syracuse, merger) and 1853 (R&S -> New York Central, consolidation). The NYC era is split again at 1883 for GEOMETRY only (Mill St approach vs ending at the main-line junction), same company and colour. Finger Lakes Rail Experience (2025-) is a separate company; 1958-2025 stays a gap. Not split: the 1850 merger with the Rochester and Syracuse Direct company (same operator); Penn Central / Conrail / Finger Lakes Railway (freight only, nothing drawn).
metadata.excluded: Not drawn: (a) all freight after 18 May 1958 - Victor - Pittsford to 1960, Canandaigua - Victor to 1978, Pittsford - Rochester to 1982, Auburn - Canandaigua to the present (Rule 1); the Ontario Central's Victor stub (freight); (b) Finger Lakes Railway's own excursions 1995-2024 - none dated or routed (report block [13], drawable NONE); (c) Pennsylvania Railroad (Northern Central) through trains Canandaigua - Rochester over this track c.1900 - undated (block [14], drawable NONE); (d) the Waterloo - Martisco excursion of 24 Oct 2026, not yet run at the research date and east of Auburn; (e) Auburn Road trains over the NYC main line from the Brighton junction into Rochester station 1883-1958 - shared main-line track.
not_yet_sourced: Opening of Geneva: Sept 1840 (Wikipedia introduction) vs by July 1841 (McKelvey; consistent with the Courier's 'first opened ... to Canandaigua'). Drawn 1841.
Rochester - Canandaigua opening day: 10 Sept 1840 departure / 12 Sept arrival (Palmer) vs 19 Sept 1840 (Wikipedia). Same year.
NYC consolidation effective date in 1853 not checked; exact 1883 date of the move from Mill St to the St Paul St station not sourced.
18 May 1958 rests on Palmer 2005 and LVRHS; the PSC order (Star-Gazette 8 May 1958) was seen only as a summary, and the 10 Oct 1958 NYC timetable cited by Wikipedia was not seen.
Headways before 1948 are entirely unsourced; every headway_min here is an estimate.

Rule 2: the original 1840-1883 at-grade approach through Rochester (Central Ave) is drawn on the post-1883 elevated alignment; whether the A&R's 1840 route between Pittsford and Brighton matches the later branch is unverified (1841 mileages run 0.7-2.3 mi long).
Rule 2: 1841 Cayuga Lake timber bridge vs the modern causeway - same line or relocated? Not checked.

Finger Lakes Rail Experience: exact turn-back points (Aurelius placed by Fowler mileage), whether each 2025 Canandaigua / Geneva trip ran the whole stretch, and 2026 as an [OPEN] last-confirmed year for Waterloo - Aurelius.
PRR (Northern Central) through trains Canandaigua - Rochester over the Auburn Road: start and end years unknown (McKelvey 'c.1900'; ended before Sept 1951).
Finger Lakes Railway excursions 1995-2024: none dated or routed.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 28.98 mi, Mill St depot - Canandaigua, against 29 mi documented when first opened (Rochester Courier 1881 via Palmer 2004) and 28.3 mi by the later NYC mileage (Fowler) - within 0.1 mi of the 1840 figure. RULE 2 - LATER ALIGNMENT IN ROCHESTER: this feature runs to the original Rochester terminus, the A&R / NYC Mill Street depot on the WEST bank of the Genesee (used 1840-1883, Fowler), ending at the Mill St crossing just short of State St. The 3.68 mi from the Brighton junction to Mill St is drawn on the present CSX Rochester Subdivision, i.e. the 1882-83 elevated alignment, standing in for the original at-grade line: the original approach ran along today's Central Avenue (beside the later elevated line) and crossed East Avenue at the Can of Worms site (Wikipedia, uncited) and crossed the Genesee 'a few rods above the Great Falls' (Palmer 2004), which matches the present bridge's position, but no survey of the at-grade line was found (OpenHistoricalMap has nothing here) and its offset from the drawn line is unknown, probably tens of metres along Central Ave. Also unverified: whether the 1840 line between Pittsford and Brighton followed the later branch route - the 1841 mileages (29 mi to Canandaigua, 63 to Seneca Falls) run 0.7-2.3 mi longer than the NYC figures. No straight-line approximated legs. Way composition of the full Mill St - Auburn trace (77.1 mi before simplification): NYC Auburn Road ways 70.6 mi (Canandaigua Line 24.6, Auburn Secondary 24.2, Auburn Trail 14.5, abandoned 'Auburn Branch' 6.6, unnamed/other 0.7); CSX Rochester Subdivision (NYC main line) 3.6 mi, Rochester only; untagged rail 1.6 mi (a 0.8 mi parallel yard/spur track through Geneva, a 0.5 mi spur beside the Auburn Trail at Victor - the surviving Victor stub - and short pieces at the Brighton junction); 0.7 mi of the Frog Pond and Erie Canalway trails at Pittsford, standing in for a lifted piece of the grade where it crosses the canal; 0.3 mi of short connectors and a 0.14 mi OHM piece at Brighton bridging gaps in the relation. Zero miles on the Lehigh Valley (Phelps / Clifton Springs / Shortsville / Victor) or on the Rochester and Eastern interurban (Victor / Fishers / Pittsford). No straight-line approximated legs. Mileposts on the drawn line from the Brighton junction vs Fowler's NYC mileage (Brighton 99.1): Pittsford 5.2 (4.6), Victor 15.5 (15.1), Canandaigua 25.5 (25.1), Geneva 48.1 (47.6), Seneca Falls 58.0 (57.5), Cayuga 62.6 (62.2), Auburn 73.2 (73.0) - waypoints are town centres, so a few tenths of a mile either way is position, not error.

segments.note: Auburn and Rochester Railroad, first section. First train left Rochester Thu 10 Sept 1840 behind the locomotive 'Lion' and reached Canandaigua Sat 12 Sept (Palmer 2004 quoting the Ontario Repository, 16 Sept 1840; first timetable published 8 Sept 1840); Wikipedia gives 19 Sept 1840 - same year. Steam from the first train; no animal-power years (horses only shunted coaches to the depot in Rochester). Rochester terminus the A&R depot on Mill Street, west bank of the Genesee (Fowler: 'Rochester (R&A, Mill St.)(1840>1883)'). Ends 1 Aug 1850, when the A&R merged with the Auburn and Syracuse to form the Rochester and Syracuse - an operator change, not a service end; the boundary year is shared with the Rochester and Syracuse feature. headway_min 320 is an ESTIMATE from McKelvey's 'three daily trains' in 1841 (Rochester History 1968); no timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: Palmer 2004 (Rochester Courier 1881; Ontario Repository 16 Sept 1840) for the 1840 opening; Wikipedia and Palmer 2005 for the 1 Aug 1850 merger; Fowler (x = 1851 Dinsmore) for the Mill St terminus; McKelvey 1968 for 'three daily trains'. Headway an estimate.

segments.note: Auburn and Rochester Railroad, eastward extension via Shortsville, Clifton Springs, Phelps, Geneva, Waterloo, Seneca Falls and the Cayuga Lake bridge to Auburn, where from Nov 1841 it met the Auburn and Syracuse and completed the Albany - Buffalo rail chain. Start collapsed to 1841: the road 'when first opened' was only the 29 mi to Canandaigua (Courier 1881 via Palmer 2004); Geneva 'by the next July' (McKelvey 1968), Seneca Falls 9 June 1841 (Wikipedia) and 'the present termination of the road' on 4 Aug 1841 (Rochester Democrat via Palmer 2004), Cayuga 18 Sept 1841 (Wikipedia), Auburn 4 Nov 1841 (Wikipedia; McKelvey; Courier 'In November, 1841'). CONFLICT recorded: Wikipedia's introduction puts Geneva in Sept 1840, against its own body and the Courier - same drawn year only if collapsed to 1841, which is what is drawn; the Canandaigua - Geneva part may have opened a little before Auburn was reached, all within 1841. Steam throughout. Ends 1 Aug 1850 (merger into the Rochester and Syracuse). headway_min 320 is an ESTIMATE ('three daily trains' 1841, McKelvey).
sources: Segment-level: Palmer 2004 (Courier 1881; Rochester Democrat 4 Aug 1841; Roman Citizen 16 Nov 1841); Wikipedia (uncited, internally inconsistent); McKelvey 1968 (Geneva July 1841, Auburn 4 Nov 1841). Headway an estimate.

segments.note: New York Central Auburn Road, Syracuse - Auburn - Geneva - Canandaigua - Rochester, from the move to the elevated main-line approach in Rochester (1883, Fowler; month not sourced) - Rochester trains used the St Paul St station 1883-1914 and the Central Ave station from 1914. McKelvey (1968) says Auburn trains were cut from 3 to 2 in the early 1940s, and that the PSC refused NYC's request to drop them in 1948. No section was cut back before 1958 in any source read. headway_min 360 is an ESTIMATE from McKelvey's three trains each way; no timetable of 1883-1947 was read.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: Fowler line 120 dates the 1883 Rochester station change and McKelvey gives the early-1940s 3-to-2 cut, but no timetable has been checked against this segment's years or headway. Supporting references for the line:

segments.note: NYC public timetable of 25 Apr 1948, Table 51 'Auburn Road', lists every station Syracuse - Auburn - Cayuga - Seneca Falls - Waterloo - Geneva - Oaks Corners - Phelps - Clifton Springs - Shortsville - Chapin - Canandaigua - Victor - Fishers - Pittsford - Brighton - Rochester (102.3 mi), with at least two trains each way daily plus a Geneva - Syracuse extra except Sundays (via Wikipedia). The Official Guide's Table 65 (Dec 2 1951) prints times for Rochester, Brighton, Shortsville 8:29, Clifton Springs 8:38, Phelps 8:47 and Oaks Corners f8:53 (flag), and the PRR Table 155 box shows the NYC train Rochester 7:10 - Canandaigua 8:02 - rail, not motor coach. One train a day by the 16 Feb 1958 timetable, still calling at Cayuga, Seneca Falls, Waterloo, Geneva, Oaks Corners (eastbound), Phelps, Clifton Springs, Shortsville, Chapin, Canandaigua, Victor and Pittsford (Wikipedia). Last passenger train 18 May 1958 (Palmer 2005; LVRHS), after the PSC authorised abandonment of passenger service Syracuse - Rochester on 10 days' notice (Elmira Star-Gazette 8 May 1958, seen as a summary only). Freight continued: Victor - Pittsford to 1960, Canandaigua - Victor to 1978, Pittsford - Rochester to 1982, and Auburn - Canandaigua to this day (Penn Central, Conrail, Finger Lakes Railway from 1995) - none of that is drawn. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE spanning 2 a day (1948) and 1 a day (1958).
sources: Segment-level: NYC timetable 25 Apr 1948 Table 51; Official Guide Feb 1952 Table 65 and PRR Table 155 box; Wikipedia (Auburn and Syracuse Railroad, citing NYC timetables of 16 Feb 1958 and 10 Oct 1958); Palmer 2005 and LVRHS for 18 May 1958. Headway an estimate.
